extracted.intended_audience: WSFS / Worldcon members, prospective Hugo Award nominators and voters, and Worldcon administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and eligibility rules governing nomination and final-ballot voting for the Hugo Awards (including use of NomNom, mail-in ballots, membership eligibility, deadlines, and category-trial procedures). Intended to guide members in making nominations, voting, and accessing voter materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-vote eligibility (LAcon V members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone who is an Attending, Online (Virtual), or World Science Fiction Society (WSFS) member of LAcon V prior to the close of voting is eligible to vote in the 2026 Hugo Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only LAcon V WSFS members will be able to vote on the final ballot and choose the winners for the 2026 Awards. If you used a different convention membership to nominate (e.g., Seattle Worldcon 2025), you will not be able to use that account to vote and must set up/use your LAcon account instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting submission methods and ballot-editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Votes can be submitted through our online balloting system, NomNom, or by mailing in a printable ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use NomNom, you can edit your ballot as often as you like until the close of the voting period. If you encounter issues, contact hugo-help@lacon.org for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting deadline / close of voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting will close on August 8, 2026 at noon PDT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to NomNom and to the Voter Packet ends when voting closes. Ballots submitted by other years/conventions follow their published deadlines (examples on the site show comparable deadlines for 2025/2024 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: NomNom account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to use NomNom you will first need to create an LAcon V virtual convention account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LAcon V members who nominated should already have an account set up. If you joined too late to nominate you will have received an email with instructions on how to set up your account. Note that a membership from another Worldcon (e.g., Seattle 2025) cannot be used to vote on LAcon V final ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hugo Awards Voter Packet availability
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also use NomNom to download the Hugo Awards Voter Packet. This resource is provided to allow Hugo Award voters to make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Packet is compiled from works donated by rights holders. Access to the Packet ends when voting closes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating eligibility and nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: WSFS members of the 2026 Worldcon (LACon V) and 2025 Seattle Worldcon as of January 31, 2026 are eligible to make up to five equally weighted nominations in each category of the Hugo Awards, as well as the Lodestar Award and the Astounding Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to nominate in all categories, nor do you need to make the maximum number of nominations in any or all categories. Those works/people who receive sufficient nominations will go on to the final ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating ballot receipt deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All ballots must be received by Saturday, March 28, 2026, 12:00 (Noon) Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper ballots are accepted but must be received by the deadline. The site includes parallel examples for 2025 (deadline March 14, 2025) and earlier years; follow the specific year’s published deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and contact responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Hugo Awards are administered by LACon V, not by the Hugo Awards web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address any questions about the 2026 Hugo Awards to the Hugo Awards Administrators of LACon V at hugo-help@lacon.org. Please do not submit questions to the Hugo Awards website, as they do not administer the awards and can only pass questions on to the award administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Poem category trial and ratification process
rubrics_metrics.description: LAcon V used their authority under Section 3.3.20 of the WSFS Constitution to present a Hugo Award for Best Poem as part of the 2026 Hugo Awards, continuing a trial begun in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running the category for an additional year is intended to provide data about its long-term viability before the WSFS Business Meeting decides whether to ratify the amendment and add Best Poem as a permanent Hugo Award category. Best Poem will be on the nominating ballot alongside permanent categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership-date-based nominating eligibility for trial category
rubrics_metrics.description: All WSFS members of the 2025 and 2026 Worldcon as of the end of January 2026 will be eligible to nominate works for the 2026 Awards (including Best Poem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the general nominating eligibility rules tying eligibility to membership as of a specific cutoff date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot validity and natural-person requirement (disqualification example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions may disqualify ballots which they rule were not cast by natural persons (example: Glasgow 2024 disqualified 377 ballots they ruled were not cast by natural persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballots ruled invalid (for reasons such as not cast by natural persons or being late) are excluded from the counted totals; the site reports counts of valid electronic and paper ballots after disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of awards administered and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hugo Awards, the Lodestar Award, and the Astounding Award are presented at a formal ceremony at Worldcon (dates/times published by the administering Worldcon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners are announced at the convention’s awards ceremony (examples: 2026 awards presented on Sunday evening, August 30, 2025 at LAcon V; 2025 presented on August 16, 2025 at Seattle Worldcon 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominator and voter statistics reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The administering Worldcon reports statistics on nominating and final ballots (e.g., number of valid nominating ballots, number of nominations, number of works/individuals nominated across categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site posts include nominators and nominations counts (e.g., 'members cast 1,488 valid nominating ballots... made 23,543 nominations for 4,299 works and individuals across 21 categories'), which inform transparency about the process.
